findings.text: The declared control's headline sum is arithmetically off: the report states 'Sum of the ten: 90.57 s = 50.6 % of the 178.98 s wall', but the ten per-test durations listed in the table above it (21.92, 14.45, 13.08, 7.70, 6.47, 5.89, 5.79, 5.41, 5.03, 5.03, transcribed verbatim from suite_head.log's --durations=25 block) sum to 90.77 s, i.e. 50.72 %, not 90.57 s / 50.6 %. The same 90.57 s figure is carried into the manifest's landing line and artifacts line ('the ten slowest are 90.57 s (50.6 %)'). The error does not change any conclusion: the ten still account for about half the wall time, the remainder is still the same per-row-commit mechanism, and the control ('reach 80 % or say where the remainder went') is met either way, so the report's account of where the remainder is spent stands. It is a transcription slip in the one number the control is named for, and a later reader who re-adds the table gets a different figure than the text.

justifications.durability: The attribution is essentially the stated mechanism, and it does not travel outside the report/recommendation it lives in. The central claim is falsification-tested -- removing the per-row commit in a scratch plugin makes the heaviest file fall from >=80.5 s in-suite to 9.29 s -- which is the right shape for a causal claim rather than merely consistent with one. Docked for: the batched experiment covers only one of the four test files (test_agent_telemetry_watch.py), so the 'suite ~30 s' expectation is an extrapolation that was never run against the whole suite; the batched run is not load-matched (load 5.68 vs 17.04 for the suite), a confound the report states plainly but which leaves the 9.29 s vs 80.5 s pair measuring load as well as the two arms and the claim resting on the load-independent micro-control; and the '5.03-21.92 s per-test variance tracks fleet fsync latency' claim is argued from the mechanism rather than measured against fsync timing.
justifications.evidence: Every clause was re-derived in this reviewer's own reads from the commits' object store and the node's logs: suite_head.log is a complete arm (108 passed, EXIT=0, no FAILED); the responsible line telemetry_index.py:1284 is present and wraps the row INSERT in 'with self._conn:'; the ingest's other commit points are :1026 (per-source) and :1050 (final) as the report's recommendation cites; the call-site attributions hold (test_agent_telemetry_watch.py:109 _index -> index.ingest(discover(directory)); :192-195 the 40-row _index; test witness); repro_timing.log shows every read <=4 ms; repro_profile.log shows 3.725 s of 3.796 s in Connection.__exit__; repro_sqlite_control.log shows 2.387 s vs 0.053 s vs 0.005 s; experiment_batched.log shows 22 passed in 9.29 s at load 5.68. The base/head code-identity claim is exactly right (git diff eb801719 539a09cb -- imas_ambix tests is empty). Docked for finding 1: the control's headline sum is stated as 90.57 s whereas the ten durations in the table sum to 90.77 s (50.7 %), a transcription slip that does not change any conclusion.
justifications.fit: The report sits in the plan's §10 support lane -- a cost attribution the §10 gpu-watch work and the written recommendation feed -- and reads as an investigation rather than a changelog: the mechanism is stated at the line that causes it (:1284), the falsification is named as such, and the recommendation is a single-file change with its blast radius bounded (insert SQL, keys and duplicate handling unchanged; only durability granularity moves, optionally bounded). Artefacts are the raw logs, not prose about logs; the report avoids plan/sprint identifiers in its text; ruff is not in play (no source changed). The only blemish is finding 1, a one-number arithmetic slip, which is why fit is docked a point rather than being maximal.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The delivered report answers the dispatched question -- why the four watch/telemetry test files take minutes -- with a single, correctly-located mechanism and a measured falsification, and it also supplies the actionable recommendation (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1284). The evidence is a real A/B on the driver rather than a hypothesis. What keeps it from the top score is that the headline recommendation ('suite ~30 s from 179 s') is an estimate extrapolated from one file and a lower-load batched run, honestly labelled as an estimate, rather than a measured suite result. Nothing in the goal is left unanswered.
